gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-palmyren: Pixel-era and a bit wistful, Visitor draws its gaping e and short ascenders over big bowls, while Noto Sans Palmyrene follows in a plain sans whose curves stop short of closing. Retro up top, modern below.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-pau-cin-: Noto Sans Pau Cin Hau keeps its curves open and its capitals low. Visitor's uniform, unshaded outline gives the heading a nostalgic digital hum that the sans body quietly lets breathe around it.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-phagspa: Retro screen glow, with Visitor's stems like dowels and arcs like bent dowels leading the way. Noto Sans PhagsPa follows in a plain sans with see-through openings, and it takes a generous size so those gaps can show.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-phoenici: Visitor's stroke edges run parallel through every curve, giving it a pixel-age, nostalgic look. Noto Sans Phoenician answers with s shapes opening wide at both ends and tall lowercase, so the sans body feels modern against that wiry heading.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-psalter-: Nostalgic, with Visitor's curves holding their thickness right through the turns and its e gaping wide. Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi has its own open e and barely rising capitals, so the two sit side by side like old friends from different decades.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-rejang: Chunky retro screen lettering, since Visitor has no pressure swells to slow the eye anywhere. Noto Sans Rejang carries a longer read in sans-serif letters with wide, porthole-like counters, so the text stays clear.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-runic: Visitor's r, n and m have arches that match their stems, which gives it a rigid, digital-age snap. Noto Sans Runic does the quieter work, with a big x-height and curves that never close back on themselves in a sans body.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-samarita: Noto Sans Samaritan reads sturdy and approachable, with a hefty lowercase and plenty of daylight inside its curves. Visitor above it has no calligraphic swell on any downstroke, and the heavy sans-serif text stays easy going down a page.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-saurasht: Wire-thin and nostalgic, Visitor looks like a monoline skeleton. It is made for striking headings, while Noto Sans Saurashtra, a sans with barely taller capitals and open counters, is built to carry the text.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-sharada: Noto Sans Sharada reads open and bulky, its c forms never closing into rings. Visitor holds a steady line with no pressure variation for punchy display work, and the plain sans handles everything that needs to be read.
